11/02/2019

Dr Christine Hodges
2 Hill Forest Road
Newtown

Dear Dr Hodges,
Re: Mr John Aloisius

I am writing to discharge Mr Aloisius from our Emergency Department back into
your care. Your further management would be highly appreciated.

On 01/02/2019, Mr Aloisius presented complaining of tuberculosis symptoms.
Examination revealed cachexia and scattered rales. A chest x-ray result showed
apical infiltrates, and a sputum acid-fast stain and a mycobacterial culture
confirmed the diagnosis of tuberculosis. As a result, he was placed in respiratory   Deleted: on
isolation and tuberculosis medications were started, including isoniazid 5mg/kg
four times daily, rifampin 10 mg/kg one time per day, pyrazinamide 15-30             Commented [RB1]: This can be expressed as ‘once’.
mg/kg four times a day, ethambutol 2.8g twice weekly and vitamin B-6 50 mg
once daily.

Today, Mr Aloisius’s sputum acid-fast stain was negative indicating good
progress. Regarding his discharge plan, the drug regimen with vitamin B-6 will
continue for four months. However, pyrazinamide and ethambutol will be ceased
after two months. He requires monitoring of his medication compliance,               Deleted: ensuring
reduction of the regimen above to 2-3 times a week after two weeks of the initial    Commented [RB2]: Above is an adverb, not an
dose, toxicity monitoring, baseline and periodic serum uric acid assessments,        adjective. Thus, it is not used before nouns.
periodic visual acuity and red-green color perception tests.                         Deleted: above


In light of the information above, your continuous care and follow-up of Mr
Aloisius’s condition would be greatly valued. If you require any further
clarification, please do not hesitate to get in contact.                             Commented [RB3]: Possibly a little informal. Try:
                                                                                     …hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Doctor

Comments
             Hawazen
             The purpose has been established sufficiently and the content is
             relevant and extended, so well done. Ideally, look to establish the
             purpose clearly in the introduction which will then leave the
             conclusion as a more generic statement. Linguistically, error free
             sentences are evident despite some scattered errors with word
             order and prepositions. Use the live grammar classes and online
             resources on the OET online website to assist with reviewing these
             items. If you require further clarification, please feel free to contact
             me.

             Focus Areas:
                • Prepositions




Overall Grade: B (around 360)
